kurz: How €125 of net pay forgone becomes a contribution of €287, and what part of it is lost again in the payout phase through income tax and health and long-term care contributions.

bloecke.md:
The occupational pension (betriebliche Altersversorgung, bAV) is a legal relationship between employer and employees and not a separate financial product. Section 1(1) BetrAVG (Occupational Pensions Act) defines it as a commitment by the employer to provide old-age, invalidity or survivors' benefits on account of the employment relationship. For this classification, it is of secondary importance who provides the money. If the employer pays, this is called an employer-funded occupational pension. If employees give up part of their gross pay, this is called [[Salary sacrifice (Entgeltumwandlung)|salary sacrifice (Entgeltumwandlung)]]. Under Section 1a(1) BetrAVG, there is a legal entitlement to salary sacrifice of up to 4% of the contribution assessment ceiling (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze) of the pension insurance. The employer decides on the funding vehicle (Durchführungsweg) but cannot refuse salary sacrifice as such.

Under Section 1(1) sentence 3 BetrAVG, the employer is liable for the promised benefit even if a third party provides it. If a Pensionskasse cuts its benefits, the former employer must make up the difference. This [[Employer's ultimate liability (Einstandspflicht)|ultimate liability (Einstandspflicht)]] distinguishes a company pension legally from a private savings contract. It also explains why the funding vehicle is above all a balance sheet question for the employer. For employees, by contrast, the choice of vehicle is about costs and investment.

bloecke.md:
## Limits in the accumulation phase

The contribution assessment ceiling (BBG) of the general pension insurance is €101,400 a year in 2026, that is, €8,450 a month. Two limits depend on it; they differ and are often confused.

Contributions to direct insurance, a Pensionskasse or a Pensionsfonds remain free of wage tax (Lohnsteuer) under Section 3 no. 63 EStG up to 8% of the BBG, which is €8,112 a year or €676 a month. Up to 4% of the BBG, that is, €4,056 a year or €338 a month, they are also free of social security contributions (Section 1(1) sentence 1 no. 9 SvEV, Social Insurance Remuneration Ordinance). In between lies a range of €4,056 a year in which no wage tax is due, but the full social security contribution is. Employees who use this range save only the tax. They still pay health and long-term care contributions on the resulting pension in old age. This constellation is the least favourable and almost always a mistake.

€8,112 a year is tax-free, and €4,056 of it is also free of contributions. Above 4% of the BBG, every euro converted costs the full social security contribution in the accumulation phase and is charged contributions a second time in the payout phase.

The advantage of salary sacrifice arises because two deductions disappear at the same time. In 2026, the employee's share of social security contributions is 9.3% in pension insurance and, in health insurance, 7.3% plus half of the average additional contribution of 2.9%, that is, 8.75%. In long-term care insurance it is half of 3.6%, making 19.85% in total. Unemployment insurance is not yet included; it increases the advantage further. In addition, there is the wage tax saved at the personal marginal tax rate. For simplicity, the illustrative calculation bases it on the full gross amount sacrificed. Because the pension, health and long-term care contributions saved would otherwise be deductible as provision expenses (Vorsorgeaufwendungen), the tax saving is smaller when calculated precisely.

schritte.name: less pension, health and care contributions

bloecke.titel: Contribution per euro of net pay forgone
bloecke.md:
Sacrificing €250 of gross pay costs €125.37 net. The €250 goes into the contract, together with the statutory employer top-up (Arbeitgeberzuschuss) of 15%, that is, €37.50. Together this makes €287.50.

The ratio is 287.50 ÷ 125.37 = 2.29. One euro of disposable income thus becomes €2.29 of contributions. A portfolio funded from taxed money first has to make up this head start. It is the main reason why the occupational pension comes out ahead in many cases despite its disadvantages.

The top-up has been mandatory since 2019 for new commitments and since 2022 for all existing commitments. Section 1a(1a) BetrAVG requires 15% of the converted pay, to the extent that the employer saves social security contributions through the conversion. This restriction has practical consequences. If the salary is above the health insurance contribution assessment ceiling of €5,812.50 a month, the employer saves no contributions there and may reduce the top-up. Collective agreements may deviate from this, including downwards. In negotiations with the employer, it is more worthwhile to talk about the amount of the top-up than about the choice of funds. Every additional percentage point of top-up takes effect immediately and without investment risk.

bloecke.md:
## Taxes and contributions in the payout phase

Some of the taxes and contributions that are not incurred in the accumulation phase fall due in the payout phase. For tax purposes, this is consistent. Because the contributions were never taxed, the benefit is taxed in full as other income (sonstige Einkünfte) under Section 22 no. 5 sentence 1 EStG. This corresponds to the usual deferred taxation and, taken on its own, is usually an advantage, because the marginal tax rate in retirement is as a rule lower than during working life.

In social security, the situation is different. The company pension counts as pension-type income (Versorgungsbezug) under Section 229 SGB V (Social Code Book V, health insurance). Under Section 248 SGB V, the full general health insurance contribution is due on it, that is, 14.6% in 2026 plus an average additional contribution of 2.9%, around 17.5% in total. The pensioner bears this contribution alone; there is no employer half. On top of this comes long-term care insurance at 3.6%, or 4.2% for childless people aged 23 and over. In total, this is around 21.1%. This burden is called the [[Double contribution charge (Doppelverbeitragung)|double contribution charge (Doppelverbeitragung)]]. Saving is done out of gross pay, and contributions are charged once more on the payout.

The only relief is an allowance, and only in health insurance. In 2026, €197.75 of pension-type income a month remains free of contributions, which is one twentieth of the reference value (Bezugsgröße) of €3,955 (Section 226(2) SGB V). In long-term care insurance, instead of an allowance there is only an exemption threshold (Freigrenze) of the same amount. If it is exceeded, the entire company pension is subject to contributions. In addition, the allowance only applies to pensioners who are compulsorily insured in the health insurance for pensioners (KVdR). Voluntarily insured persons pay contributions from the first euro.

serien.name: Health and care insurance as a percentage of the gross pension

bloecke.md:
Health and long-term care contributions are also due if the capital is paid out as a lump sum. Section 229(1) sentence 3 SGB V notionally spreads the sum over 120 months. For ten years, a 120th of it counts as monthly pension-type income.

With capital of €171,000, that is €1,425 a month. The health insurance contribution is (1,425 − 197.75) × 17.5% = €214.77, the long-term care contribution 1,425 × 3.6% = €51.30. Together that makes €266.07 a month, and €31,928 over 120 months. This corresponds to around 18.7% of the payout, even before income tax is applied.

## Effects on the pension and wage replacement benefits

Salary sacrifice reduces the pay subject to pension insurance contributions. As a result, fewer earnings points (Entgeltpunkte) are credited. Sickness benefit (Krankengeld), unemployment benefit (Arbeitslosengeld) and parental allowance (Elterngeld) are also lower, because they are all based on gross pay subject to contributions.

A permanent conversion of €250 a month reduces annual pay subject to contributions in 2026 by €3,000. With provisional average earnings of €51,944, that is 0.0578 fewer earnings points a year. With a current pension value (aktueller Rentenwert) of €42.52, this corresponds to €2.46 less monthly pension for each year of conversion. Over 25 years, this adds up to around 1.44 earnings points or just over €61 of statutory monthly pension. The calculation is static; future adjustments of average earnings and the pension value are not taken into account.

If the same conversion produces capital of €171,000, this capital must yield more than the €61 of monthly pension forgone. An annuity conversion factor (Rentenfaktor) of around €3.60 per €10,000 is enough for this, and offers customary in the market are well above that. The loss of earnings points is a real disadvantage, but it rarely tips the balance of the decision.

## Occupational pension and ETF portfolio compared

A fair comparison starts from the same net outlay, not the same gross contribution. €125.37 of net pay forgone a month results in a contribution of €287.50 in the occupational pension, and an investment of €125.37 in the portfolio.

bloecke.md:
The calculation assumes a return of 5% a year and 300 monthly contributions for both variants. The occupational pension incurs no product costs; the portfolio holds an equity ETF with 30% partial exemption. Not taken into account are the advance lump sum, which favours the portfolio, and the saver's allowance (Sparerpauschbetrag), which puts it at a disadvantage.

- The occupational pension reaches €287.50 × 595.5 (future value annuity factor) = around €171,000 of capital.
- The portfolio reaches €125.37 × 595.5 = around €74,700, of which €37,600 are payments and around €37,050 is gain. The tax is 70% × €37,050 × 26.375% = €6,840. Around €67,800 remains net.

Tax and contributions are due on the occupational pension capital in the payout phase. With a total burden of 35%, around €111,000 remains, with 45% around €94,000, both considerably more than in the portfolio.

Calculated the other way round, with a 40% burden in the payout phase, the result of the occupational pension only falls to €67,800 net if it earns just over 2% return a year. The head start therefore offsets costs of around three percentage points a year. That is a lot, but with an expensive contract without a significant top-up, the head start is used up.

bloecke.titel: Salaries above the health insurance contribution ceiling
bloecke.md:
A monthly salary of more than €5,812.50 is above the contribution assessment ceiling for health and long-term care insurance. No health or long-term care contributions are levied on pay above this ceiling anyway, so salary sacrifice no longer saves anything there. Contributions to pension and unemployment insurance continue to be saved up to €8,450, but health and care insurance contributions do not.

In the payout phase, the full health and long-term care contribution is still due on the company pension. These employees therefore bear the burden in the payout phase without having saved health and long-term care contributions in the accumulation phase. What remains is the tax advantage, for example a marginal tax rate of 42% today compared with perhaps 25% in retirement. Arithmetically, the conversion can then still pay off, but the margin is small. In addition, the employer top-up may be lower in this situation, because it is limited to the contributions saved.

schritte.titel: Ask about the amount of the top-up
schritte.text: Find out whether the employer pays only the statutory 15% or more. Any top-up above that immediately shifts the calculation in favour of the occupational pension.

schritte.titel: Determine your position relative to the limits
schritte.text: Below €5,812.50 gross a month, the full advantage applies. Above that, the saving on health and care insurance disappears.

schritte.titel: Convert at most 4% of the BBG
schritte.text: The limit for freedom from contributions is €338 a month. Converting more than that is rarely worthwhile.

schritte.titel: Request the reduction in yield in writing
schritte.text: What counts is the reduction in yield of the entire contract; the fund costs alone are not enough.

schritte.titel: Compare the expected company pension with the allowance
schritte.text: If the pension is close to €197.75, the contribution burden is low. From €800, you should allow for just under 17%.

schritte.titel: Further saving in a securities account
schritte.text: The subsidised amount is limited. Anything you want to save beyond it can go into a securities account.

bloecke.titel: Second Occupational Pensions Strengthening Act from 22 January 2026
bloecke.md:
- The **social partner model** (Sozialpartnermodell) is a pure defined contribution commitment without a guarantee, but in return it allows a higher equity allocation. It is now also open to companies not bound by a collective agreement if they join an existing collective agreement.
- An **opting-out** system is possible by works agreement. Employees are then enrolled automatically and must actively object if they do not want to take part.
- The settlement limits for **very small entitlements** (Kleinstanwartschaften) rose from 1.0% to 1.5% of the monthly reference value, that is, in 2026 to around €59.33 of monthly pension or €7,119 of capital. With the employees' consent, such entitlements can be paid into the statutory pension insurance.
- The **subsidy for low earners** (Förderbetrag, Section 100 EStG) rises from €288 to €360 a year from 2027. The wage threshold is linked to 3% of the contribution assessment ceiling; its exact value in euros had not been clearly documented at the editorial deadline.

The double contribution charge remained unchanged.

Two points are often overlooked in the tax discussion. The first is **vesting** (Unverfallbarkeit). Entitlements from salary sacrifice vest immediately under Section 1b(5) BetrAVG, employer-funded ones only after the commitment has existed for three years and the employee has reached the age of 21. If employment ends before this point, they lapse.

The second is **adjustment**. Section 16 BetrAVG obliges the employer to review current company pensions for adjustment every three years. For direct insurance and a Pensionskasse, this obligation does not apply if all surpluses are used to increase the benefit. Many company pensions therefore remain constant in nominal terms and lose value in real terms every year. A company pension promises a nominal amount and does not protect against inflation.

mitnehmen: In the model case, €125 of net pay forgone becomes a contribution of €287.50; this factor of around 2.3 is the main advantage of the occupational pension and offsets around three percentage points of annual costs before an ETF portfolio draws level.
Contributions are tax-free up to 8% of the contribution assessment ceiling, but only free of social security contributions up to 4%; the range in between is the least favourable option.

In the payout phase, income tax under Section 22 no. 5 EStG and around 21.1% health and long-term care contributions are due, which the pensioner bears alone; in 2026 only €197.75 a month remains free in health insurance, and in long-term care insurance there is no allowance, only an exemption threshold of the same amount.
A lump-sum payout is also subject to contributions, because Section 229(1) sentence 3 SGB V notionally spreads it over 120 months.

The decision depends on three quantities: the amount of the employer top-up, your own pay relative to the contribution assessment ceiling of health insurance, and the reduction in yield of the contract offered.

begriffe.text: Giving up part of gross pay in favour of an entitlement to a company pension. There is a legal entitlement to it up to 4% of the contribution assessment ceiling (Section 1a(1) BetrAVG), and the conversion is tax-free up to 8% (Section 3 no. 63 EStG).

Legal form in which the pension commitment is implemented, that is, direct pension commitment, support fund, direct insurance, Pensionskasse or Pensionsfonds. The funding vehicle determines the limits of state support, the investment of capital and insolvency protection.
Liability of the employer for the promised benefit, even if a third party provides it (Section 1(1) sentence 3 BetrAVG). It distinguishes the company pension from a private contract.

Charging a company pension financed from gross pay with the full health and long-term care insurance contribution in the payout phase, which the pensioner bears alone. In 2026, this is around 21.1% above the health insurance allowance of €197.75.

Income comparable to a pension within the meaning of Section 229 SGB V, for example a company pension, a pension from a professional pension scheme or a civil servant's pension. As a rule, the full health insurance contribution is due on it, which the pensioner bears alone; for company pensions, an allowance of €197.75 a month applies to compulsorily insured persons in 2026. Lump-sum benefits are notionally spread over 120 months and charged contributions for ten years.
